scenes.title: The Motto on the Brass
scenes.summary: At nine-thirty Wednesday morning, F1 and M1 carry the rescued oval brass plaque back from Clock-Square Pavilion and read its warm founding motto with M2.
scenes.intro: At half past nine Wednesday morning, {F1} and {M1} stride triumphantly through the lobby door carrying a heavy cloth bundle, where {M2} waits with his reading glasses firmly on his nose. Listen first.
story: M2
Let me see it! Did the archive cabinet key turn without sticking, {M1}?
M1
Turned like butter, boss—and our neighbour signed the return book as official witness.
F1
Watch me fold back the green velvet cloth... behold our founding oval brass plaque!
M2
Solid cast brass, thirty centimetres wide, with four countersunk screw holes around the rim!
M1
Give me ten seconds with this lemon-oil cloth to brighten the lower engraving.
F1
Oh, look at the letters emerging beneath {M1} and his polishing rag!
M2
Read the motto aloud slowly, {F1}, so I savour every historic syllable!
F1
It says: Warm bread, quiet shade, and an open gate make strangers into friends.
M2
Warm bread, quiet shade, and an open gate—that describes {SHOW} to perfection!
M1
Notice it says nothing about white cotton gloves or velvet ropes, boss.
F1
Can we screw it back onto the limestone gate arch right after lunch, {M1}?
M1
First I set four fresh lead anchors in the stone so it stays forever.
scenes.outro: Rescued after ten years behind glass, the oval brass motto captures the exact soul of {SHOW}! See you in the kitchen next time.

scenes.title: Honey Fig Almond Twists
scenes.summary: Inspired by the plaque's warm-bread motto, F2 unveils her signature Festival Honey-Fig and Spiced Almond Twists with help from M4 and F1.
scenes.intro: In the fragrant café corner at eleven, {F2} pulls a golden baking sheet from the oven while {M4} and {F1} lean in over braided spirals of pastry. Let us listen in first.
story: F1
{F2}, what is that heavenly aroma filling the entire ground floor right now?!
F2
Meet our official Saturday Festival Pastry: Braided Honey-Fig and Spiced Almond Twists!
M4
I chopped forty dried golden figs and roasted a full kilo of sweet almonds!
F2
Rolled inside warm cinnamon dough, braided into neat rings, and brushed with orange-blossom honey.
F1
Wait—no forks or plates needed, so walking festival guests can hold one in a napkin!
F2
Smart AND crumb-proof, {F1}! You think like a true café partner now!
M4
How many braided twists can our two ovens turn out for Saturday morning, Chef?
F2
Sixty fresh twists before ten in the morning, plus forty more at two!
F1
Did Chief Judge {M1} give his official carpenter-pencil score yet?
F2
Here comes his verdict right now—hide the extra tray or none will survive!
M4
Wait—what is that giant cardboard parcel {M2} is dragging behind {M1}?!
F1
Uh-oh, whenever {M2} drags a tall box into the kitchen, stand clear!
scenes.outro: Braided honey-fig twists win instant applause—just before {M2} arrives dragging a mysterious tall parcel! See you next time.

scenes.title: No Screwdriver Needed
scenes.summary: While M1 praises F2's braided twists, M2 insists on assembling a tall three-tier brass pastry stand by hand without letting M1 tighten the centre rod.
scenes.intro: Setting a tall square carton beside the café counter, {M2} beams proudly at {F2} and {M1}. Listen first.
story: M1
Before we discuss your mysterious box, boss: {F2}, that fig twist is eleven out of ten.
F2
ELEVEN OUT OF TEN?! {M1} just broke his own mathematical scale!
M2
An eleven-point pastry deserves a royal stage—behold our Three-Tier Brass Display Tower!
F2
Ooh, three round brass plates stacked high so sixty twists shine on the counter!
M1
Hand me the centre threaded rod and the bottom hex nut, boss; I have my wrench.
M2
Put your wrench away, {M1}! The box clearly says Easy Hand Assembly in Two Minutes!
M1
Boxes say all kinds of cheerful fibs when nobody uses a proper steel washer.
M2
Bottom tier on, brass pillar twisted finger-tight, middle tier on, top crown spun!
F2
Wait, {M2}—why is the top plate leaning slightly toward the teapot?!
M2
Artistic perspective, {F2}! Load twenty warm honey twists onto all three levels!
M1
Keep two clean trays ready in your hands, {F2}—gravity never reads the box.
F2
Twelve twists on the bottom, eight in the middle, six on top... nobody breathe!
scenes.outro: Finger-tight brass meets twenty-six warm pastries as {M1} quietly prepares for gravity to win! See you next time.

scenes.title: The Leaning Tower of Pastries
scenes.summary: Seconds after M2 steps back to admire his hand-tightened stand, the centre rod unscrews—and F1 and F2 pull off a diving two-tray rescue without dropping a single pastry!
scenes.intro: {F1} walks into the café corner carrying clean linen napkins at the exact instant {M2}'s tall three-tier brass tower begins a slow, graceful spin to the left. Listen to the whole scene first.
story: M2
Observe, {F1}: effortless elegance, zero tools, ready for any Festival Judge in {CITY}!
F1
Um, {M2}... is the top tier supposed to rotate counterclockwise by itself?!
F2
The centre rod is unscrewing! {F1}, grab that wide baking tray on your left!
M2
Stay upright, Brass Tower! I command you as owner and manager of {SHOW}!
F1
Diving right for the top six twists—got one, two, three, four, five, six!
F2
Sweeping left under the middle plate—all eight caught cleanly on parchment paper!
M2
And I have the wobble—clink—well, I caught the decorative brass acorn finial!
F1
Twenty-six honey-fig twists safe, warm, and untouched by the counter or the floor!
F2
{F1}, with reflexes like yours, you could play goalkeeper for {CITY}!
M2
Clearly the factory cut those brass threads backward in metric millimetres!
F1
Or somebody skipped the steel lock washer sitting right here inside the cardboard flap!
M2
Take the lock washer straight to {M1}, ladies, and never speak of that acorn!
scenes.outro: Twenty-six pastries survive without a scratch thanks to championship café reflexes—and the lock washer heads straight to {M1}! See you next time.

scenes.title: Sawing the Cedar Frames
scenes.summary: Out in the courtyard workshop corner after five, M3 and M4 join clean cedar corners with wooden dowels while F3 tests the linen fabric density.
scenes.intro: Late Wednesday afternoon under the courtyard shade tree, {M3} and {M4} set up two wooden sawhorses with their family carpentry tools while {F3} inspects a bolt of heavy oatmeal linen. Listen first.
story: F3
How satisfying to watch two brothers build something musical with hand tools!
M4
Grandfather kept this brass-backed tenon saw sharp for forty years, {F3}.
M3
Slide that corner joint together, {M4}—mortise and wooden dowel, zero metal squeaks!
F3
Feel the weight of this natural unbleached linen we found at the fabric market.
M3
Hold it up to your mouth and hum middle D through the weave, {F3}.
F3
Mmm—warm air passes gently through while sharp high echoes soften right down!
M4
If we stretch two layers over each cedar frame, they will look like sunlit screens!
M3
And {M1} already tightened that brass pastry tower with two lock washers inside.
F3
Goodness, did the famous tool-free tower try to take flight at lunch?!
M4
{F1} caught six pastries mid-air while {M2} rescued one tiny brass acorn!
F3
Never a dull afternoon on {STREET}! How many cedar screens remain to assemble?
M4
Frame two is done now, and frames three and four will stand ready by noon tomorrow!
scenes.outro: Mortise-and-dowel cedar frames take shape smoothly in the hands of the two brothers ahead of Thursday! See you next time.

scenes.title: Lock Washer Magic
scenes.summary: In the quiet early-evening kitchen, M1 bolts the three-tier brass stand rock solid for F2 and adds rubber pads beneath its feet.
scenes.intro: Inside the tidy café corner at six, {M1} sets the gleaming three-tier brass pastry stand back onto the counter before {F2} and gives the top ring a firm tap. Let us listen in first.
story: M1
Go ahead and push the top plate with two fingers, {F2}—try to make it wobble.
F2
Not a millimetre of play! What did you do underneath the base, {M1}?
M1
Toothed steel lock washer, brass hex nut, and three cork pads glued under the feet.
F2
Cork pads too, so it never scratches my wooden counter or slides when full!
M1
You worked too hard inventing those honey-fig twists to play goalkeeper on Saturday.
F2
Honestly, {M1}, when I opened this four-table corner, I never imagined hosting a city festival.
M1
Four tables or forty tables, people come here because your bread tastes like home.
F2
Careful, {M1}—two compliments in one Wednesday and people will think you went soft!
M1
Purely protecting my own Saturday morning breakfast supply, Chef.
F2
Speaking of Thursday deliveries, {F1} warned me {M2} accidentally ordered a giant cloth banner!
M1
How giant can one street welcome sign possibly be?
F2
Four metres wide by two metres tall—keep your pocketknife handy tomorrow!
scenes.outro: Rock-solid brass and cork feet guard Saturday's pastries—while Thursday's four-metre delivery looms down {STREET}! See you next time.

scenes.title: Drilling the Limestone Anchors
scenes.summary: At the street gate after supper, M1 cleans out the four original screw holes in the limestone arch while F1 and M3 test the alignment of the oval brass plaque.
scenes.intro: Cool Wednesday twilight settles along {STREET} as {M1} brushes stone dust from the four original holes beside the gate arch while {F1} holds the gleaming oval plaque and {M3} checks his spirit level. Listen first.
story: M3
Raise the right edge two millimetres, {F1}... bubble dead centre in the glass tube!
F1
Look how the oval brass rim fits the faint shadow on the limestone to the millimetre!
M1
Good nineteenth-century masons drilled straight and deep; my new bronze anchors slide right home.
F1
Shall we screw the plaque onto the wall tonight or wait until Friday evening, {M1}?
M1
Wait until after {M2} finishes whatever circus he planned with that giant banner.
M3
Wise call—nobody wants a four-metre cloth sail snagging fresh bronze screws!
F1
Read the polished words under the streetlamp one more time, {M3}.
M3
Warm bread, quiet shade, and an open gate make strangers into friends.
F1
Look across the street: two neighbours walking their dog already stopped to smile!
M1
Wrap the plaque back in velvet for tonight and lock it inside the front-desk drawer.
M3
Tomorrow afternoon we test all four linen acoustic screens with piano AND violin!
F1
Provided we can still find the front gate behind that four-metre cloth banner!
scenes.outro: Four bronze anchors wait cleanly in the limestone while the polished plaque sleeps safe until Friday! One final scene in Episode 3!

scenes.title: A Roll Like a Carpet
scenes.summary: First thing Thursday morning, two delivery men carry a four-metre canvas cylinder into the lobby, leaving M2 insisting it will look majestic across the gate arch.
scenes.intro: Eight sharp Thursday morning at {SHOW}! {F1} and {M4} press flat against the front-desk counter as {M2} directs a canvas roll the length of a rowing boat straight through the lobby doorway. Listen first.
story: M2
Mind the umbrella stand, mind the brass bell—set it gently along the hallway rug!
M4
Good grief, {M2}, did you buy a spare mainsail from a tall ship?!
F1
It stretches all the way from the front door to the kitchen swinging arch!
M2
Do not exaggerate, {F1}; once hung high outdoors, large scale projects confidence!
M4
Wait—our stone gate arch is only two and a half metres wide, {M2}!
F1
Where are the extra one hundred and fifty centimetres of banner supposed to go?!
M2
Graceful draped folds on both sides, like velvet curtains at the municipal opera house!
M4
And if the banner is two metres tall in a two-metre doorway, how do guests enter?!
M2
Details, {M4}, minor geometric details we shall solve outside after breakfast!
F1
Look at the dark grey cloud drifting behind the clock tower right now, gentlemen...
M4
Sun-shower cloud plus four square metres of heavy canvas—call {M1} immediately!
M2
Onward to the gate arch—{SHOW} is going on the map in giant letters!
scenes.outro: Four metres of canvas march out toward a two-and-a-half-metre gate under a drifting rain cloud! End of Episode 3—see you in Episode 4!
